sampling_model.design: Observational two-period binary panel with exact inversion of the sixteen-cell law.
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent units drawn from the population law \(P\).
sampling_model.treatment: The binary predetermined covariate \(X_t\) is not randomized. Initial assignment and the feedback distribution of \(X_2\) after \((X_1,Y_1)\) may depend arbitrarily on \(u\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every observed cell is positive. The weak latent model permits zero assignment or feedback probabilities; the strict latent model requires almost-everywhere positivity, with no numerical lower bound. Observed-cell positivity alone does not imply the strict latent condition.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The cell law is estimated by multinomial frequencies. Whole-set inversion uses simultaneous Clopper--Pearson marginal intervals, while fixed-slope endpoint estimation projects frequencies onto the relevant attainable affine hull.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.1 characterizes the identified set by conditional moment equalities with generalized moments in a truncated Stieltjes cone.
Theorem 1 characterizes all feedback and heterogeneity robust moment conditions for the common parameter.
The main theorem replaces a latent distribution by a finite-dimensional identification-equivalent distribution for discrete covariates.

body.tldr: For a two-period binary logit panel with a predetermined binary covariate and unrestricted heterogeneity taking values in the continuous state space \((0,\infty)\), the model-generated joint slope--APE fibers equal finite quartic Stieltjes feasibility sets for every observed probability vector, including zero-cell laws. The heterogeneity law may be atomic, absolutely continuous, or mixed. Eight coupled response-type measures preserve one unconditional law and reconstruct legal history-conditioned sequential kernels without a cross-world independence assumption. The weak certificate has fifty-six variables with eight \(3\times3\) and eight augmented \(4\times4\) PSD blocks; strict almost-everywhere assignment and feedback positivity has sixty-four variables and eight further \(6\times6\) common-range blocks. Universally, \(\operatorname{sign}(\Delta)=\operatorname{sign}(\theta)\) for \(\theta\ne0\) and \(|\Delta|\le\tanh(|\theta|/4)\), with equality exactly at \(\mu=\delta_{e^{-\theta/2}}\). Downstream results give sharp fixed-slope endpoint programs with separate attainment tests, terminating algebraic membership and projection, exact multinomial whole-set coverage, and pointwise endpoint consistency only at relative-interior attainable laws.

project_justification.gap: Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham characterize the sharp \(T=2\) unrestricted-feedback model conditional on \(X_1\) by an infinite-dimensional program and compute the unrestricted-support case with grids. Dobronyi, Gu, Kim, and Russell provide truncated-Stieltjes tools for a different conditional structure, but do not reconstruct a separately unknown heterogeneity-dependent feedback kernel from one unconditional mixing law. Neither comparison supplies the sharp universal envelope \(|\Delta|\le\tanh(|\theta|/4)\) together with this exact joint fiber.
project_justification.niche: At two periods, a product coupling of the two feedback-coordinate marginals creates eight joint response types as a construction, without asserting cross-world independence. The binary-logit path likelihoods share a positive quartic denominator, so five bounded generalized moments per type suffice; common Hankel range is exactly what upgrades separate open-half-line representability to a shared finite positive-node support with every type weight positive.
project_justification.fill: The note proves two-sided maps between independently defined weak and strict legal sequential models, eight response-type measures, and finite Stieltjes lifts on the entire observed-law simplex. When \(q_x>0\), normalization of \(h_xd\mu\) and the reverse mixture \(\mu=\sum_xq_x\pi_x\), \(h_x=d(q_x\pi_x)/d\mu\), identify the weak lift with the Bonhomme--Dano--Graham unrestricted-measure fiber. The strict fiber is an additional subclass, and no equivalence to a separately imposed Lebesgue-density specialization is claimed. The cone also yields the sharp universal slope--APE envelope and supports endpoint, algebraic-decision, exact-coverage, and fixed-slope relative-interior results.

body.related_work: Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham (2023), Proposition 1 and Sections 5.1--5.3, provide the sharp \(T=2\) unrestricted-feedback program conditional on \(X_1\) and its unrestricted-support grid implementation. After adjoining \(q_x\), the present weak model has the same unrestricted-measure fiber via \(\pi_x(E)=q_x^{-1}\int_Eh_xd\mu\) and the reverse formulas \(\mu=\sum_xq_x\pi_x\), \(h_x=d(q_x\pi_x)/d\mu\). This statement concerns arbitrary probability measures on the continuous state space \((0,\infty)\), not continuous densities; equivalence to a Lebesgue-density specialization would need an additional absolutely-continuous representation theorem, which the atomic converse does not supply. The strict initial-and-feedback-positive fiber is an additional subclass rather than a second Bonhomme--Dano--Graham Proposition 1 fiber. Dobronyi, Gu, Kim, and Russell (2026), Theorems 3.1--3.2, provide rational-mixture and truncated-Stieltjes ideas, but their model does not contain the separately unknown unrestricted feedback kernel reconstructed here. Curto and Fialkow (1991) and Bayer and Teichmann (2002) provide classical moment and finite-atomic substrate. Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham (2026) study feedback-robust moment equalities, while Gu, Russell, and Stringham (2026) use finite latent-cell enumeration; neither supplies this continuous-logit legal-kernel equivalence. Arellano and Carrasco (2003) provide the predetermined-children labor-participation design that can consume the exact bounds.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The strict common-support proof is existential and does not provide an efficient atom-extraction algorithm. Real quantifier elimination terminates for algebraic inputs but carries no polynomial complexity or numerical-stability guarantee. A closed lifted PSD set can have a nonclosed linear image, so fixed-slope infima and suprema need separate endpoint-attainment tests. Relative-interior convex continuity does not extend automatically to attainable boundary laws, changes of Hankel rank, or the observable-map rank loss at \(c=1\).
body.honest_scope: The proved contribution is the exact finite-certificate equivalence for the independently defined two-period binary weak and strict fibers. Its proved ingredients are the forward joint-response construction, reverse legal-kernel reconstruction under the history-conditioned sequential logit restriction, and the common-support certificate required for strict positivity. The equivalence covers arbitrary probability laws on the continuous heterogeneity state space \((0,\infty)\), including atomic and mixed laws, and all observed probability vectors; positive \(q_x\) is used only for the conditional-on-\(X_1\) Bonhomme--Dano--Graham comparison. That comparison is exact for the weak unrestricted-measure fiber after adjoining \(q_x\); the strict fiber is an additional subclass, and exact correspondence with a Lebesgue-density specialization is not established. The note also proves the sharp universal slope--APE envelope, sharp fixed-slope endpoints with separate inclusion tests, algebraic membership and projection, conservative exact multinomial whole-set inversion, and pointwise endpoint consistency for fixed \(c\) at relative-interior attainable laws. Uniform inference on rank-changing faces, continuity outside \(\operatorname{ri}(C_c^v)\), and joint consistency as \(c\) approaches one remain open, as do certified extraction, arbitrary \(T\), restricted feedback dynamics, and multinomial outcomes.
body.interpretation: The finite cone is an identifying map for the independently defined causal slope--APE fiber, not a regression estimand or a discretized outer approximation. The universal inequality \(|\Delta|\le\tanh(|\theta|/4)\) is an outer envelope for any fixed observed law and is sharp when admissible laws vary; equality for nonzero slope requires all unconditional heterogeneity mass at \(u=c^{-1/2}\). Weak cone feasibility permits type measures with different supports. Strict feasibility is stronger: the common-range blocks certify a representation on one positive-node set with every response type receiving positive weight, exactly what makes all reconstructed initial and feedback probabilities positive almost everywhere.
